product_problems: Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem
Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem

mdr_text.text: IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY RIGHT UPPER LOBECTOMY PROCEDURE, THE 8MM CURVED-TIP SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT FIRED A GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD ON THE PULMONARY ARTERY AND THE STAPLE LINE OOZED SOME BLOOD. THE SURGEON REPORTEDLY DID NOT PERFORM ANY INTERVENTION DUE TO THIS EVENT AND THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. INTUITIVE SURGICAL INC. (ISI) CONTACTED THE SURGEON OF THIS PROCEDURE AND ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WAS OBTAINED ABOUT THE COMPLAINT: THE SURGEON SAID THE OOZING FROM THE STAPLE LINE WAS TYPICAL AND EXPECTED. THE SURGEON EXPLAINED THAT BLEEDING NORMALLY OCCURS WITH STAPLERS ON SMALL BLOOD VESSELS. THE SURGEON SAID THEY WOULD HAVE NORMALLY DIVIDED THIS VESSEL WITH ENERGY APPLICATION, BUT DECIDED TO USE THE 8MM CURVED-TIP SUREFORM 30 STAPLER WITH A GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD SINCE THEY WERE TESTING THIS DEVICE. THE SURGEON CLARIFIED THAT THE STAPLER INSTRUMENT AND RELOAD USED DURING THIS FIRE WORKED WELL AND THAT THEY DID NOT PERFORM ANY ACTIONS TO RESOLVE THE OOZING. THE SURGEON SAID THIS EVENT HAD NO IMPACT OF THE PROCEDURE OUTCOME NOR THE PATIENT OUTCOME. THE PATIENT WAS NOT REPORTEDLY HOSPITALIZED LONGER THAN THEY WERE EXPECTED TO, AND HAVE BEEN DISCHARGED.

BASED ON THE INFORMATION PROVIDED, THE CAUSE OF THE REPORTED COMPLICATION CANNOT BE DETERMINED. THE GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD USED DURING THIS EVENT WAS REQUESTED FOR RETURN, BUT HAS NOT BEEN RECEIVED AT THIS TIME. A FOLLOW-UP MDR WILL BE SUBMITTED IF ADDITIONAL INFORMATION IS OBTAINED. A SYSTEM LOG REVIEW WAS PERFORMED FOR THIS PROCEDURE: NO RELEVANT ERRORS WERE OBSERVED DURING THIS PROCEDURE. AN ISI FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER (FAE) REVIEWED THE STAPLER LOGS FOR THIS EVENT. PER THE FAE, THE LOGS SHOW THAT 8MM CURVED-TIP SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT (PART #488530-10, LOT #U90220315-0004) WAS INSTALLED 13 TIMES AND FIRED 12 RELOADS (4 BLUE FOLLOWED BY 1 GRAY FOLLOWED BY 2 WHITE FOLLOWED BY 5 BLUE, IN THAT ORDER). ALL FIRINGS WERE COMPLETED PER THE LOGS. THE FIRST 7 FIRINGS HAD NO PAUSES FOR COMPRESSION, AND THE LAST 5 FIRINGS HAD 1 OR 2 PAUSES. THERE WERE NO INCOMPLETE CLAMPS BY THIS INSTRUMENT. THIS COMPLAINT IS BEING REPORTED DUE TO THE FOLLOWING CONCLUSION: DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY LOBECTOMY PROCEDURE, THE 8MM CURVED-TIP SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT FIRED A GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD ON THE PULMONARY ARTERY AND THE STAPLE LINE OOZED SOME BLOOD. NO MEDICAL INTERVENTION WAS ADMINISTERED DUE TO THE OOZING AND THE SURGICAL PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. FOLLOW-UP WAS ATTEMPTED, BUT THE MISSING PATIENT INFORMATION WAS EITHER UNKNOWN, UNAVAILABLE, NOT PROVIDED, OR NOT APPLICABLE. THE EXPIRATION DATE IS NOT APPLICABLE. THE PRODUCT IS NOT IMPLANTABLE. IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE INITIAL REPORTER SUBMITTED A REPORT TO THE FDA.

A CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER REVIEWED THE VIDEO OF THIS PROCEDURE AND PROVIDED THE FOLLOWING OBSERVATIONS: "FROM THE GIVEN VIDEO IT LOOKS LIKE AT AROUND 5:20 AND AT 6:03 THERE WERE TWO EVENTS OF MINOR OOZING OF BLOOD FROM THE STAPLE LINES AFTER A FIRE WITH THE 8MM SUREFORM 30 CURVED STAPLER. THE OOZING WAS RESOLVED BY ITSELF. I AM UNABLE TO DETERMINE WHY THE OOZING OCCURRED FROM THIS VIDEO ALONE. THE OOZING OBSERVED IS NOT SPECIFIC TO DA VINCI STAPLERS AND CAN OCCUR IN ANY STAPLING PROCEDURE. IN THE VIDEO, WE DO NOT SEE ANY MALFORMED STAPLES AND WITH THIS VIDEO ALONE, WE ARE UNABLE TO DETERMINE THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE MINOR OOZING AND AIR LEAK. "
REFER TO H10/H11 FOR FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION.

Detachment of Device or Device Component

mdr_text.text: THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE INCOMPLETE STAPLE LINE IS DUE TO A STAPLER MALFUNCTION. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE BROKEN FRAGMENT HAS NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED YET. A FOLLOW-UP MDR WILL BE SUBMITTED IF ADDITIONAL INFORMATION IS RECEIVED. INTUITIVE HAS RECEIVED THE PART ASSOCIATED WITH THIS COMPLAINT AND COMPLETED INVESTIGATIONS. FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATIONS CONFIRMED THE CUSTOMER REPORTED COMPLAINT. THE RELOAD WAS FOUND TO HAVE UNDEPLOYED PUSHERS. ONE SIDE OF THE RELOAD WAS FOUND TO BE FULLY DEPLOYED, WHILE THE OTHER SIDE ONLY HAD ONE PUSHER DEPLOYED. THE ONE PUSHER WAS FOUND AT THE MOST PROXIMAL END OF THE RELOAD. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE IS ATTRIBUTED TO COMPONENT FAILURE. ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS NOT REPORTED BY THE SITE WERE ALSO IDENTIFIED. A FRAGMENT WAS RETURNED ALONG WITH THE RELOAD. THE FRAGMENT RETURNED IS FROM A DRIVER OF A SUREFORM 30. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE WAS NOT ESTABLISHED AND WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO ENGINEERING FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION. NO IMAGE OR VIDEO CLIP FOR THE REPORTED EVENT WAS SUBMITTED FOR REVIEW. A REVIEW OF THE SYSTEM AND INSTRUMENT LOGS HAS BEEN PERFORMED. THERE WERE NO OBSERVED EVENTS IN THE AVAILABLE SYSTEM LOGS THAT WOULD SUGGEST A PRODUCT ISSUE, AND LOGGED EVENTS ARE IN LINE WITH NORMAL SYSTEM FUNCTIONALITY. A REVIEW OF THE ADVANCED STAPLER LOG REVIEW FOR THE SUREFORM STAPLER ASSOCIATED WITH THIS EVENT HAS BEEN PERFORMED BY AN INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) FAE. THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WAS PROVIDED: LOGS SHOW PN 488530-10, LOT U10220706-0112 WAS INSTALLED ONCE WITH A GRAY RELOAD. CLAMPING AND FIRING WERE COMPLETED PER THE LOGS, AS WAS THE UNCLAMP EVENT. THERE ARE NO ERRORS IN THE MSC LOGS RELATED TO THE 8MM SF 30 INSTRUMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THE 8MM SF30 RELOADS NO LONGER CONTAIN A KNIFE. THE KNIFE HAS BEEN INTEGRATED INTO THE INSTRUMENT, AS PART OF THE NEW ¿DRIVER¿ COMPONENT (I-BEAM + SHUTTLE + KNIFE COMBINED). THIS COMPLAINT IS BEING REPORTED DUE TO THE FOLLOWING CONCLUSION: DURING THE FIRST FIRE OF THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER, WHICH WAS INSTALLED WITH A GRAY RELOAD, THE STAPLER DID NOT FIRE PROPERLY. THE STAPLER ONLY PUT DOWN STAPLES ON ONE SIDE OF THE STAPLE LINE WHEN FIRING ON THE SEGMENT BRANCH OF THE PULMONARY VEIN. THE STAPLE LINE WAS LEFT OPEN ON THE SPECIMEN SIDE AND 50 ML OF BLOOD WAS LOST FROM THE SPECIMEN SIDE AS A RESULT. THE SURGEON APPLIED PRESSURE, CLIPS AND SUTURED THE VEIN TO CONTROL THE BLEEDING. A FRAGMENT FROM THE DRIVER OF THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER WAS ALSO FOUND TO HAVE FALLEN INTO THE PATIENT WHICH THE SURGEON RETRIEVED USING A 3RD PARTY LAPAROSCOPIC INSTRUMENT.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY SEGMENTECTOMY SURGICAL PROCEDURE, WHEN THE CUSTOMER FIRED THE 8 MM SUREFORM 30 STAPLER WITH A GRAY RELOAD, THE STAPLE LINE DID NOT LAY DOWN AND THE STAPLER ¿KNIFE¿ FELL INSIDE THE PATIENT. THE SURGEON WAS ABLE TO RETRIEVE THE FRAGMENT IN THE SAME PROCEDURE WITH A BACKUP INSTRUMENT. THE CUSTOMER COMPLETED THE CASE WITH A SUREFORM 45 STAPLER. THE CUSTOMER DISCARDED THE STAPLER AND WOULD RETURN THE RELOAD ONLY. THE FRAGMENT DID NOT FALL INTO THE PATIENT DURING AN INSTRUMENT COLLISION. INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) FOLLOWED UP WITH THE SURGEON AND OBTAINED THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION : THE ISSUE OCCURRED ON THE FIRST STAPLER FIRE OF THE PROCEDURE. THE SURGEON WAS FIRING ON THE SEGMENT BRANCH OF THE PULMONARY VEIN. THE STAPLER CLAMPED NORMALLY AND FIRED. THE GREY RELOAD ONLY FIRED ONE SIDE OF THE STAPLE LINE. THE SIDE THAT FIRED WAS COMPLETED WITHOUT ANY MISSING OR MALFORMED STAPLES. NONE OF THE STAPLES ON THE OTHER SIDE FIRED AT ALL. THERE WERE NO OBSTRUCTIONS, AND THE TISSUE WAS IN NORMAL CONDITION. THE STAPLE LINE WAS LEFT OPEN, AND THE PATIENT LOST 50CC OF BLOOD IN 2 SECONDS FROM THE SPECIMEN SIDE. TO ADDRESS THE BLEEDING, THE SURGEON APPLIED PRESSURE, APPLIED CLIPS, AND SUTURED THE TISSUE. NO BUTTRESS MATERIAL WAS USED. AFTER THAT, THE SURGEON FOUND THAT THE BLADE FROM THE RELOAD HAD FALLEN INTO THE PATIENT. THE BLADE WAS REMOVED WITH A LAPAROSCOPIC INSTRUMENT AND VISUALLY CONFIRMED BY THE SURGEON THAT THERE WERE NO OTHER FRAGMENTS. NO X-RAYS OR ANY OTHER TESTS WERE PERFORMED. THE SURGEON COMPLETED THE PROCEDURE WITH A BACKUP SUREFORM 45 STAPLER WITH NO FURTHER ISSUES. THE PATIENT HAS NOT RETURNED TO THE HOSPITAL WITH ANY POST-SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. THE SURGEON REPORTED THAT THERE IS A PROCEDURE VIDEO, HOWEVER IT IS NOT AVAILABLE TO ISI FOR REVIEW.
REFER TO H10/H11 FOR FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION.

ON 07-DEC-2022, INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) RECEIVED THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE DEVICE EVALUATION OF THE SUREFORM 45 STAPLER INSTRUMENT. FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATION HAS BEEN COMPLETED AND THE ROOT CAUSE HAS BEEN DETERMINED. THE ROOT CAUSE FOR THE DRIVER WEDGE BEING DEFORMED UPWARDS WAS HANDLING OF THE DRIVER, BETWEEN COMPONENT MANUFACTURING AND INSTRUMENT ASSEMBLY. THIS UPWARDS DEFORMATION CAUSED THE DRIVER WEDGE TO CONTACT THE PUSHERS ABOVE THE PUSHER RAMP UPON FIRING THE INSTRUMENT, WHICH RESULTED IN STAPLES NOT DEPLOYING ON ONE SIDE OF THE CUT LINE. AS THE FIRING PROGRESSED, THE DRIVER WEDGE WAS ABNORMALLY LOADED, CAUSING A MECHANICAL OVERLOAD FAILURE. THIS FAILURE CAUSED THE WEDGE TO FRACTURE AND GENERATE A FRAGMENT.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY SEGMENTECTOMY PROCEDURE, THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT FIRED A GRAY RELOAD ON THE LUNG, BUT THE STAPLE LINE DID NOT COMPLETELY STAPLE THE TISSUE. BLEEDING OCCURRED AND WAS RESOLVED WITH HEM-O-LOK CLIP APPLICATION. LOOSE STAPLES WERE RETAINED IN THE PATIENT. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. POST-OPERATIVELY, THE PATIENT¿S PLAN OF CARE WAS NO DIFFERENT THAN INITIALLY PLANNED. INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) HAS MADE MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS TO CONTACT THE SURGEON OF THIS PROCEDURE TO OBTAIN ADDITIONAL INFORMATION; HOWEVER, AS OF THE DATE OF THIS REPORT, NO FURTHER DETAILS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED. FOLLOW-UP: ON 10/07/2022, ISI CONTACTED THE SITE ROBOTICS COORDINATOR AND ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WAS OBTAINED ABOUT THE COMPLAINT: THE SURGEON FIRED A GRAY RELOAD AND IT "MISSED" THE TARGET TISSUE CAUSING SOME BLEEDING. THE BLEEDING WAS RESOLVED WITH A ROBOTICALLY PLACED HEM-O-LOK CLIP. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. THE CUSTOMER SAID SHE WAS NOT PRESENT, BUT WAS INFORMED BY THE STAFF IN THE ROOM AT THE TIME. THERE WAS NO ALLEGATION OF THE TARGET TISSUE BEING PUSHED OR MOVING UNEXPECTEDLY, RATHER, THE STAPLER SOMEHOW STAPLED TISSUE THAT WAS NOT INTENDED TO BE STAPLED.

BASED ON THE INFORMATION PROVIDED, THE CAUSE OF THE REPORTED COMPLICATION HAS BEEN DEEMED TO BE PRODUCT RELATED. ISI RECEIVED THE GRAY RELOAD (1) INVOLVED WITH THIS COMPLAINT AND COMPLETED THE DEVICE EVALUATION. UPON VISUAL INSPECTION, THE RELOAD WAS RETURNED USED AND FIRED. THERE WAS CARTRIDGE DAMAGE OBSERVED IN TWO LOCATIONS. THERE WAS DAMAGE SEEN ON BOTH SIDES OF THE DISTAL END. THERE WAS NO MISSING MATERIAL. A REVIEW OF LOGS SHOWED NO FIRING FAILURES. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE USER. A FOLLOW-UP MDR WILL BE SUBMITTED IF ADDITIONAL INFORMATION IS OBTAINED. ISI RECEIVED THE OTHER GRAY RELOAD (2) INVOLVED WITH THIS COMPLAINT AND COMPLETED THE DEVICE EVALUATION. UPON VISUAL INSPECTION, THE RELOAD WAS RETURNED USED AND FIRED. THERE WAS CARTRIDGE DAMAGE OBSERVED WITHIN THE KNIFE TRACK. THERE WAS NO MISSING MATERIAL; THE DAMAGES WERE STILL INTACT. A REVIEW OF LOGS SHOWED NO FIRING FAILURES. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE USER. ISI RECEIVED THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT INVOLVED WITH THIS COMPLAINT AND COMPLETED THE DEVICE EVALUATION. FAILURE ANALYSIS DID NOT REPLICATE OR CONFIRM THE REPORTED COMPLICATION. THE STAPLER WAS TESTED IN-HOUSE AND THE INSTRUMENT INITIALIZED, CLAMPED, FIRED, AND UNCLAMPED WITHOUT ANY ISSUES ON BOTH ATTEMPTS. THE INSTRUMENT MOVED INTUITIVELY WITH A FULL RANGE OF MOTION IN ALL DIRECTIONS. THE GRIPS OPENED AND CLOSED PROPERLY. NO ERRORS APPEARED DURING IN-HOUSE TESTING. A REVIEW OF LOGS SHOWED NO FIRING FAILURES. NO DAMAGE WAS FOUND. THERE WAS NO PROBLEM DETECTED. A SYSTEM LOG REVIEW WAS PERFORMED FOR THIS PROCEDURE: NO RELEVANT ERRORS WERE OBSERVED DURING THIS PROCEDURE. THE STAPLER LOGS FOR THIS EVENT WERE REVIEWED BY A FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER: "LOGS SHOW PN 488530-10, LOT U10220708-0074 WAS INSTALLED 3X AND FIRED 2 RELOADS (BOTH GRAY). FIRINGS OCCURRED ON FIRST TWO INSTALLS. BOTH FIRINGS WERE COMPLETED PER THE LOGS WITH NO PAUSES FOR COMPRESSION. THERE WERE NO INCOMPLETE CLAMPS BY THIS INSTRUMENT. THERE WAS A 3RD INSTALL OF THIS INSTRUMENT THAT USED A BLUE RELOAD, BUT THE LOGS SHOW A COMPLETED CLAMP FOLLOWED BY A COMPLETED UNCLAMP, WITH NO FIRING ATTEMPTED." A CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER (CDE) REVIEWED THE IMAGES RECEIVED OF THIS EVENT: "WITH THE IMAGES PROVIDED, I CAN CONFIRM THAT THERE WERE MALFORMED STAPLES. HOWEVER, WITH THIS IMAGE ALONE I AM UNABLE TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THIS ISSUE." THIS EVENT IS BEING REPORTED DUE TO THE FOLLOWING CONCLUSION: IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY SEGMENTECTOMY PROCEDURE, THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT FIRED A GRAY RELOAD ON THE LUNG, BUT THE STAPLE LINE DID NOT COMPLETELY STAPLE THE TISSUE. BLEEDING OCCURRED AND WAS RESOLVED WITH HEM-O-LOK CLIP APPLICATION.

INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) HAS RECEIVED THE PART ASSOCIATED WITH THIS COMPLAINT AND COMPLETED INVESTIGATIONS. FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATIONS REPLICATED AND CONFIRMED THE CUSTOMER REPORTED COMPLAINT THE GREY RELOAD WAS DIFFICULT TO INSTALL. FAILURE ANALYSIS FOUND THE PRIMARY FAILURE OF CARTRIDGE DAMAGE TO BE RELATED TO THE CUSTOMER REPORTED COMPLAINT. THE RELOAD DID NOT SHOW ANY OBVIOUS PHYSICAL OR COSMETIC DAMAGE. HOWEVER, WHEN ATTEMPTING TO INSTALL THE RELOAD ONTO THE IN-HOUSE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER, THE RELOAD REVEALED THE CARTRIDGE WAS DAMAGED AT THE TAIL END OR PROXIMAL END NEAR THE DRIVER. THE EDGE PIECE OF THE RELOAD HOLDING THE DRIVER WAS CRACKED AND BEGAN TO BREAK DURING INSTALLATION ONTO THE STAPLER. THE RELOAD WAS UNABLE TO BE FIRED ON AN IN-HOUSE SYSTEM. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE IS ATTRIBUTED TO USER MISHANDLING, COMMONLY CAUSED BY THE IMPROPER INSTALLATION ONTO THE INSTRUMENT. FOR CLARIFICATION, FAILURE ANALYSIS FOUND THE PRIMARY FAILURE OF BROKEN RELOAD TO BE RELATED TO THE CUSTOMER REPORTED COMPLAINT. IN ADDITION TO THERE BEING A USER RELATED ASPECT AS A COMMON CAUSE OF BREAKAGE, FOR THE 8MM SUREFORM 30 RELOAD, THE DESIGN MAY ALSO BE A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR, AS THE DESIGN INCLUDES A TAIL AND OTHER FEATURES THAT NEED TO BE PROPERLY ALIGNED WITH RESPECT TO THE CHANNEL. VERIFICATION OF THE EVENT DETAILS VIA SYSTEM LOGS CANNOT BE PERFORMED SINCE FA CONFIRMED THE RELOAD WAS UNOPENED AND NOT USED DURING A PROCEDURE. NO IMAGE OR VIDEO CLIP FOR THE REPORTED EVENT WAS SUBMITTED FOR REVIEW. THIS COMPLAINT IS BEING REPORTED DUE TO THE FOLLOWING CONCLUSION: FAILURE ANALYSIS IDENTIFIED THAT A COMPONENT OF THE RELOAD EXPERIENCED A BREAK. WHILE THERE WAS NO REPORT OF HARM OR INJURY TO THE PATIENT, THE REPORTED FAILURE MODE COULD LIKELY CAUSE OR CONTRIBUTE TO AN ADVERSE EVENT IF IT WERE TO RECUR.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED THORACIC PROCEDURE, THE GREY RELOAD WAS DIFFICULT TO INSTALL. THE TIPS WERE FLIMSY AND WOULD BEND DURING INSTALLATION. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED WITH NO REPORTED INJURY.

mdr_text.text: INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) RECEIVED THE RELOAD, STAPLER 30 INVOLVED WITH THIS COMPLAINT AND COMPLETED THE DEVICE EVALUATION. FAILURE ANALYSIS (FA) INVESTIGATION CONFIRMED THE CUSTOMER REPORTED COMPLAINT OF "TIP IS FLIMSY AND BENDS WHEN INSTALLING". FOR CLARIFICATION, THE STAPLER 30 RELOAD WAS BROKEN AT THE PROXIMAL END. THERE WAS NO MATERIAL TO BE NOTED THAT APPEARED TO BE MISSING. THE RELOAD HAS NOT BEEN FIRED AT ALL. FAILURE ANALYSIS DETERMINED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE USER. VERIFICATION OF THE EVENT DETAILS VIA SYSTEM LOGS CANNOT BE PERFORMED AT THIS TIME BECAUSE THERE IS INSUFFICIENT EVENT DATE INFORMATION. NO IMAGE OR VIDEO CLIP FOR THE REPORTED EVENT WAS SUBMITTED TO ISI FOR REVIEW. THIS COMPLAINT IS CONSIDERED A REPORTABLE EVENT DUE TO THE FOLLOWING CONCLUSION: FAILURE ANALYSIS (FA) IDENTIFIED THAT A COMPONENT OF THE RELOAD STAPLER EXPERIENCED A BREAK, AND WHILE THE BREAK DID NOT RESULT IN FRAGMENTS FALLING INTO THE PATIENT, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THIS REPORTED FAILURE MODE PRESENTS A POTENTIAL HAZARD FOR FRAGMENTS FALLING THAT COULD LIKELY CAUSE OR CONTRIBUTE TO AN ADVERSE EVENT IF IT WERE TO RECUR, AS UNINTENDED BROKEN FRAGMENT(S) FALLING INSIDE THE PATIENT MAY REQUIRE SURGICAL INTERVENTION. IF ADDITIONAL INFORMATION BECOMES AVAILABLE A SUPPLEMENTAL MDR WILL BE SUBMITTED.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY LOBECTOMY SURGICAL PROCEDURE, THE RELOAD, STAPLER 30 TIP WAS FLIMSY AND BENT WHEN INSTALLING. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY WITH NO PATIENT INJURY REPORTED. FOLLOW-UP WAS ATTEMPTED TO REQUEST ADDITIONAL INFORMATION RELATED TO THE EVENT. HOWEVER, NO FURTHER DETAILS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED AS OF THE DATE OF THIS REPORT.

AN INVESTIGATION WAS COMPLETED TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THIS REPORTED EVENT. INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) DID NOT RECEIVE THE DA VINCI PRODUCT WITH AN ALLEGED ISSUE TO PERFORM FAILURE ANALYSIS. A RETURN MATERIAL AUTHORIZATION (RMA) HAD BEEN ISSUED REQUESTING TO HAVE THE ISI DEVICE RETURNED; HOWEVER, ISI DID NOT RECEIVE THE RMA TO CONFIRM/IDENTIFY THE FAILURE MODE. ALTHOUGH THE COMPLAINT WAS NOT CONFIRMED BY FAILURE ANALYSIS SINCE THE PRODUCT WAS NOT RETURNED, THE INFORMATION GATHERED INDICATES THAT THE DEVICE MAY HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE CUSTOMER REPORTED ISSUE. NO NON-CONFORMANCES WERE IDENTIFIED TO BE RELATED TO THIS COMPLAINT. A REVIEW OF THE SITE'S SYSTEM LOGS FOR THE REPORTED PROCEDURE DATE WAS CONDUCTED BY AN INTUITIVE QUALITY ENGINEER. INVESTIGATION REVEALED THERE WERE NO RELATED SYSTEM ERRORS TO HAVE OCCURRED DURING THE SURGICAL PROCEDURE THAT WOULD HAVE LIKELY CAUSED OR CONTRIBUTED TO THE REPORTED COMPLAINT. A LARGE CLIP APPLIER INSTRUMENT WAS USED 3 TIMES, ROUGHLY 20 MINUTES AFTER THE SUREFORM STAPLER 30 WAS INSTALLED. THE PROBABLE ROOT CAUSE CANNOT BE DETERMINED BASED ON THE INFORMATION PROVIDED. SINCE THE PRODUCT WAS NOT RETURNED AND THE LOG REVIEW WAS INCONCLUSIVE, THE REPORTED EVENT WAS UNABLE TO BE CONFIRMED OR REPLICATED. BASED ON THE DETAILS OF THE CUSTOMER COMPLAINT OBTAINED VIA FOLLOW-UP, HEMOSTASIS WAS ACHIEVED WITH USE OF A WECK CLIP.
REFER TO H11 FOR FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED SPLENECTOMY PROCEDURE, A STAPLE LINE BLEED OCCURRED AFTER A GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD WAS FIRED WITH A SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT. THE SURGEON WAS FIRING OVER THE SPLENIC ARTERY AND EXPERIENCED A LOT OF BLEEDING. THE CUSTOMER USED A WECK CLIP ON THE STAPLE LINE TO STOP THE BLEEDING, AS WELL AS AN ADDITIONAL CLIP ON THE PROXIMAL PORTION OF THE ARTERY. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. ACCORDING TO THE SURGEON, THE PATIENT WAS REPORTEDLY "FINE" FOLLOWING THE EVENT. INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) ATTEMPTED FOLLOW-UP TO OBTAIN ADDITIONAL INFORMATION. HOWEVER, NO FURTHER DETAILS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED AS OF THE DATE OF THIS REPORT.

AN INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER REVIEWED THE STAPLER LOGS FOR THE STAPLER INSTRUMENT USED IN THIS EVENT AND THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION WAS PROVIDED: THE LOGS SHOW SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT (PART #488530-13, LOT #U80240624-0065) WAS INSTALLED ON THE SYSTEM AND FIRED 1 GREY RELOAD. ON THE ONLY INSTALL, THE FIRST CLAMP WAS SUCCESSFUL, AND THE FIRING WAS COMPLETED WITH NO PAUSES FOR COMPRESSION. THE INSTRUMENT WAS THEN REMOVED AND NOT USED IN THE PROCEDURE AGAIN. THERE WERE NO STAPLER RELATED ERRORS IN THE LOGS.

BASED ON THE INFORMATION PROVIDED, THE CAUSE OF THE REPORTED COMPLICATION CANNOT BE DETERMINED. INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) HAS RECEIVED THE GRAY SUREFORM 30 STAPLER RELOAD AND SUREFORM 30 STAPLER FOR EVALUATION; HOWEVER, THE FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATION HAS NOT BEEN COMPLETED. AN ADVANCED STAPLER LOG INVESTIGATION BY AN INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER (FAE) REVEALED THE FOLLOWING: THE LOGS SHOW THAT THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER (PART NUMBER 488530-12), (LOT NUMBER U83240125-0153) WAS INSTALLED ON THE SYSTEM ONE TIME AND FIRED 1 GRAY RELOAD. ON THE ONLY INSTALL OF THE INSTRUMENT, THE FIRST CLAMP WAS SUCCESSFUL, AND THE FIRING PASSED WITHOUT PAUSING FOR COMPRESSION. THE UNCLAMP WAS COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT USED IN THE PROCEDURE AGAIN. THERE ARE NO ERRORS RELATED TO THE USE OF THE STAPLER.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY LOBECTOMY SURGICAL PROCEDURE, THE FIRST FIRE OF A SUREFORM 30 GREY RELOAD HAD AN INCOMPLETE STAPLE LINE WHILE STAPLING ACROSS A BRANCH OF THE PULMONARY ARTERY. THERE WERE NO COMPLICATIONS, PAUSES, OR ERROR MESSAGES DURING THE FIRING SEQUENCE. THE STAPLE LINE WAS INCOMPLETE AND MALFORMED STAPLES WERE PRODUCED. THE SURGEON RESOLVED THE DEFECT BY PLACING A CLIP AROUND THE ARTERY. THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT WAS NOT USED AFTER THE EVENT. A SUREFORM 45 CURVED-TIP STAPLER INSTRUMENT WAS UTILIZED FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE PROCEDURE, WHICH WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY WITH NO FURTHER ISSUES. THE PATIENT IS RECOVERING WELL.
REFER TO H11 FOR FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION.

AN INVESTIGATION WAS COMPLETED TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THIS REPORTED EVENT. INTUITIVE SURGICAL, INC. (ISI) RECEIVED A SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT AND GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD TO PERFORM FAILURE ANALYSIS. THE SUREFORM 30 STAPLER INSTRUMENT AND GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD ASSOCIATED WITH THIS COMPLAINT WERE ANALYZED AND THE COMPLAINT WAS NOT CONFIRMED BY FAILURE ANALYSIS. THE STAPLER INSTRUMENT WAS TESTED IN-HOUSE, AND THE INSTRUMENT INITIALIZED, CLAMPED, FIRED, AND UNCLAMPED WITHOUT ANY ISSUES. THE STAPLER INSTRUMENT FIRED SUCCESSFULLY TWICE USING TWO GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOADS. THE CUT-LINE APPEARED SMOOTH AND CONSISTENT. ALL STAPLES WERE DEPLOYED AND CORRECTLY FORMED INTO THE PROPER B-SHAPE. THERE WAS NO DAMAGE TO THE RELOAD AND NO RELATED FAILURES. THE RETURNED RELOAD WAS USED AND FIRED. A VISUAL INSPECTION DISPLAYED NO SIGNS OF PHYSICAL DAMAGE TO THE CARTRIDGE, PUSHERS, OR COVER AND THE BLADE WAS CONCEALED AT THE DISTAL END. NO PRODUCT ISSUE WAS IDENTIFIED. AS OF 11-DEC-2024, A REVIEW OF THE SITE'S COMPLAINT HISTORY DOES NOT SHOW ANY ADDITIONAL COMPLAINTS RELATED TO THIS PRODUCT AND/OR THIS EVENT. THE PROBABLE ROOT CAUSE CANNOT BE DETERMINED BASED ON THE INFORMATION PROVIDED AND FAILURE ANALYSIS RESULTS. NO PRODUCT ISSUE WAS IDENTIFIED. THE REPORTED EVENT WAS NOT CONFIRMED AS FAILURE ANALYSIS FOUND NO DAMAGE OR FUNCTIONAL ISSUE. THE RELOAD AND STAPLER WERE VISUALLY INSPECTED AND EVALUATED FOR ITS MECHANICAL AND/OR ELECTRICAL CHARACTERISTICS. THE FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATIONS AND IN-HOUSE TESTING OF THE RETURNED PRODUCT REVEALED NO ISSUES RELATED TO THE CUSTOMER REPORTED EVENT. IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED LEFT LOWER PULMONARY LOBECTOMY SURGICAL PROCEDURE, A GREY SUREFORM 30 RELOAD WAS USED TO TRANSECT THE PULMONARY ARTERY (PA) THE STAPLE LINE WAS INCOMPLETE. THE SUREFORM 30 CURVED-TIP STAPLER INSTRUMENT WORKED WITHOUT COMPLICATION PRIOR TO THE EVENT WITH BLUE RELOADS. THE STAPLER WITH THE SECOND-TO-LAST GREY RELOAD WAS LOADED INTO THE SYSTEM WITHOUT ERROR. THE STAPLER HAD A GOOD ANGLE ON THE PA. THE CLAMP WAS SUCCESSFUL WITH NO ERROR MESSAGES. DURING THE FIRING SEQUENCE WITH THE GREY RELOAD, THERE WERE NO COMPLICATIONS; THE RELOAD FIRED STRAIGHT ACROSS THE PA. ONCE THE FIRING WAS COMPLETE, THE STAPLER WAS UNCLAMPED, AND THE TISSUE WAS FULLY TRANSECTED. BLEEDING WAS IMMEDIATELY IDENTIFIED FROM THE SPECIMEN SIDE OF THE TISSUE. PRESSURE AND SUCTION WERE APPLIED FOR BETTER VISUALIZATION. THERE APPEARED TO BE NO STAPLES FORMED ALONG THE SPECIMEN SIDE OF THE PA IN THE WALL OF THE VESSEL. SOME FORMED STAPLES WERE NOTED TO BE FLOATING AROUND THE SURROUNDING AREA. THE RETAINING PATIENT SIDE OF THE PA THAT WAS TRANSECTED WAS INTACT, WITH A COMPLETE, FORMED STAPLE LINE. NO INTERVENTION WAS REQUIRED. THE PATIENT'S TISSUE INTEGRITY WAS HEALTHY; THE PATIENT WAS A NONSMOKER. THE SUREFORM 30 CURVED-TIP STAPLER WAS USED AGAIN AFTER THE EVENT WITH NO COMPLICATIONS. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. THE PATIENT WAS STABLE AND DISCHARGED HOME THE NEXT DAY. THE GRAY RELOAD TRANSECTED THE PA; HOWEVER, THE SPECIMEN SIDE OF THE STAPLE LINE WAS OPEN. THE PATIENT SIDE OF THE STAPLE LINE WAS COMPLETE. BLEEDING FROM THE SPECIMEN SIDE OCCURRED, AND REQUIRED INTERVENTION. A BLUE SUREFORM 30 RELOAD WAS FIRED AFTER THE EVENT WITH THE SAME STAPLER WITH NO REPORTED COMPLICATION. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED ROBOTICALLY. THE PATIENT IS STABLE.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT DURING A DA VINCI-ASSISTED PULMONARY SEGMENTECTOMY PROCEDURE, THE SUREFORM 30 CURVED TIP STAPLER INSTRUMENT FIRED A SUREFORM 30 GRAY RELOAD AND DID NOT COMPLETE THE STAPLE LINE. THIS OCCURRED DURING THE RESECTION OF THE MIDDLE LOBE; AFTER A SMALL BRANCH OF THE PULMONARY ARTERY WAS STAPLED. DESPITE THE STAPLE LINE APPEARING TO BE SEALED WITH THE STAPLES BEING FORMED ALL THE WAY ACROSS THE VESSEL, A SMALL AMOUNT OF BLEEDING WAS OBSERVED. THE SURGEON APPLIED PRESSURE FOR ABOUT 5 MINUTES WITHOUT SUCCESSFULLY CONTROLLING THE OOZING. THE SURGEON WAS UNABLE TO QUANTIFY THE EXACT VOLUME OF OOZING BUT ESTIMATED IT AS A 3 ON A SCALE OF 1 TO 10. COAGULATION VIA THE USE OF A LONG BIPOLAR GRASPER INSTRUMENT WAS USED TO PINCH THE VESSEL AND THE OOZING STOPPED. THE PROCEDURE WAS COMPLETED AS PLANNED. THE SURGEON CONFIRMED THERE WERE NO COMPLICATIONS FROM THE SURGERY. THE PATIENT HAD AN EXPECTED POST-OPERATIVE COURSE AND WAS DISCHARGED HOME.
